content.title: PlayStation Plus Games Hub – Every Game Available in PS Plus
content.text: PlayStation's long-running subscription service, PlayStation Plus (or PS Plus for short) has been through a lot of iterations since it was first introduced all the way back during the PlayStation 3 era. Certain things have stayed the same, like subscribers getting a few games a month added to their library with the price of their subscription, but most of it has changed, and this hub is designed to keep track of those changes. Below, you'll find lists of every game available at each tier of PS Plus subscription, including breakdowns of the different tiers and their prices. We'll also keep everything as updated as possible, as we do with our Xbox Game Pass Games Hub. Table of ContentsPS Plus Tiers (Pricing, Features)PlayStation Plus Essential - $9.99/monthPlayStation Plus Extra - $14.99/monthPlayStation Plus Premium - $17.99/monthPlayStation Plus Games (by Tier)PS Plus Essential GamesPS Plus Extra GamesPS Plus Premium Games (Classics Catalog) PS Plus Tiers (Pricing, Features) There are three subscription tiers to choose from with PS Plus. NOTE: All prices are in USD, and pricing may vary based on your region. PlayStation Plus Essential - $9.99/month Beginning with the lowest tier, PS Plus Essential is your foot in the door. It's what you get if you're not looking to have a Game Pass-style library of games, and just want to be able to play online with your friends. For $9.99/month, a PS Plus Essential subscription gets you: Monthly Games - anywhere from three to four games that you can add to your library each month, and once you add them to your library, you'll always be able to go back and play them so long as you have an active subscription Online Multiplayer - the ability to play multiplayer games online and take advantage of any game's online capabilities Exclusive Discounts - discounts on games in the PlayStation Store not available to non-subscribers Cloud Storage - the ability to keep your game save data backed up in the cloud, making it extremely easy to transfer from one console to another Share Play - the ability to invite your friends to play a game on your console by digitally passing the controller to them, or vice-versa Exclusive Content - select free-to-play games and first-party PlayStation games will sometimes include cosmetic items/DLC only available to subscribers One thing worth noting with the monthly games is that you must manually add them to your library while they are available. Each monthly batch is only available to add to your library for a limited time, and if you miss the window, you miss out on getting those games through your subscription. Next up is PS Plus Extra, the middle-of-the-road tier that, in terms of what you get for an extra $5 a month, is actually a pretty significant increase in value. That's because the main different between PS Plus Extra and PS Plus Essential is a massive library of games to play, Game Pass style, with more added every month (and, of course, some removed). Here's what a PS Plus Extra subscription gets you: Everything that comes with PS Plus Essential Game Catalog - a library of games that span across first-party and third-party titles, all playable through your subscription, with more added each month, anywhere from six to eight games Ubisoft+ Classics - a library of classic Ubisoft titles to go on top of the library of games included in the Game Catalog It's worth noting that, unlike the Monthly Games you get as part of the Essential tier, when a new batch of games is added to the Extra-tier Game Catalog, you don't have to then go manually add them to your library to access them after the month they are introduced. Like Game Pass, as long as they are part of the Game Catalog and you have an active subscription, you'll be able to download and play them. PlayStation Plus Premium - $17.99/month Lastly, the top and most expensive tier is PS Plus Premium, which, in addition to everything that comes with the previous two tiers, gives you a couple of more ways to access more games. Here's what a PS Plus Premium subscription gets you, for an extra $3 a month compared to PS Plus Extra: Everything that comes with PS Plus Essential and PS Plus Extra Classics Catalog - a catalog of PS1, PS2, PS3, PSP, and PS4 games for some retro gaming, though the PS3 games cannot be downloaded, and are almost always only playable through Cloud Streaming Cloud Streaming - the ability to stream classic PS3 titles, and also almost any of your games across all PlayStation generations, including the latest PS5 games. Game Trials - extended trials with select games so you can try them out before you buy them by playing the first few hours, in place of playing a limited demo Sony Pictures Catalog - a selection of up to 100 films subscribers can watch through the Sony Pictures Core app on your PlayStation console You should note that for most of the games in the Classic's Catalog, you can buy them individually if there are some retro titles you wish to revisit, but don't want to jump up to a whole subscription tier to have access to. It's also worth noting is that this tier works best for players who've purchased a PlayStation Portal, because you'll be able to play practically all of your PS5 games over the Cloud. In fact, if all you did was buy a PlayStation Portal and a PS Plus Premium subscription, you could have a whole library of games to play without buying a PS5 - but the moment your subscription ends, so does your access to all of those titles, especially since the Portal has no capability to play games natively. PlayStation Plus Games (by Tier) PlayStation Plus. NOTE: All games listed are included as of April 2026. New games are added and removed each month, and we will continue to update this article to keep it as accurate as possible. All games are listed alphabetically. PS Plus Essential Games This list will consistently be very short, because the games available through PS Plus Essential change each month. So, each month we'll link our coverage to the games available for the current month, as well as what was available last month, so you see what's available now and what you may have just missed - or what you could still grab, since you might get it before the new batch takes over.
